messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: high error rate for serving-runtime: CUDA_ILLEGAL_DEVICE_ADDRESS spikes on gke-inference-prod-us-east-* clusters. Auto-incident INC-2026-042 created.

alex (oncall): seeing 5xx spikes and node restarts in us-east1. metrics show deviceaddr faults ~2m ago. paging OOMs also > normal. pulling logs now.

maya (runtime): thanks alex. can you paste the pod logs for the failing replica set? I'm checking kernel oops pattern.

alex (oncall): tail from one of the crash loops: 
```
2026-03-15T13:07:12Z serving-runtime[pid=4123]: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at 0x7f4a2b1f4000
stack: runtime.c:452 kernel.c:179 kv_cache.c:88
container: pid 4123 killed by signal 11
OOM killer invoked: mmc0: oom_reaper
```

diego (serving): that looks like a device address translation error during pagewalk. we had similar symptoms but not identical. suspect a kernel race between hugepage mapping and the GPU driver when eviction happens.

katie (support): any customer impact numbers? Support is getting pings from org-omega and alpha-saas.

alex (oncall): initial telemetry: ~7% of requests errored in last 10m in us-east, ~3% increased latency. Affected deployments: text-gen-prod (3 pods), rerank-prod (1 pod). Impacting customers: org-omega (10% of its calls retried), alpha-saas (loss of long-context streams).

jenna (product): forwarding to account execs. ETA to mitigation?

maya (runtime): triage plan: 1) take affected node(s) OOS (cordon + drain) 2) disable batching on the route to reduce KV cache pressure 3) move heavy jobs to cpu-fallback pool 4) collect full vm/pci logs and kernel oops 5) if node repro, escalate to kernel/driver team for hotfix.

alex (oncall): executing now: 
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-prod-ue1-23
kubectl drain gpu-node-prod-ue1-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force\```

ops-bot: Deployment rollback triggered by alex: rolling back serving-runtime image from sha:abc1234 -> sha:ff1e00. Rollout started.

diego (serving): rollback good to try — previous image has slightly different allocator behavior. also flipping realtime flag to 0 to disable aggressive prefetching: 
```yaml
serving.runtime.featureFlags.realtimePrefetch: false
```

alex (oncall): draining node completed, new pods scheduling to other nodes. errors dropped to ~1.2% but still see occasional CUDA_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS.

maya (runtime): can you run repro on a repro node with same kernel + driver? I want to run rte-kv-cache stress with multi-tenant batching to see if we can reproduce locally.

alex (oncall): provisioning a repro node now. running stress script.

(alex runs): 
```bash
ssh repro-gpu-01
sudo journalctl -u kubelet -f | grep -E "CUDA_ERROR|illegal"
# start stress harness
./scripts/stress_kv_cache.sh --workers 64 --seq-len 4096 --batch 8
```

15m later — alex (oncall): repro loop triggered the same fault: kernel oops with pagewalk fault referencing unaligned deviceaddr (offset 0x2c). attaching kernel oops snippet: 
```
[ 3421.123456] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU_bdf: page_walk error: addr=0x7f4a2b1f4000 offset=0x2c
[ 3421.123457] BUG: kernel NULL pointer deref in pagewalk.c:line 411
[ 3421.123458] process runtime:4123 comm serving-runtime Tainted: G           N
```

maya (runtime): confirms kernel-level pagewalk NULL/deref; looks like a race when freeing page map entries while GPU still performing TLB walk. escalate to kernel/driver team. open ticket to nvidia-driver-team@internal. include repro harness and kernel oops.

diego (serving): interim mitigation suggestions: - lower batch size to 1 for heavy routes - disable prefix-level caching across requests - temporarily route long-context models to dedicated-reserved pool with newer kernel/driver combo - enable fallback to cpu for streams > 2048 tokens

alex (oncall): implementing mitigations: 
- patched route configs to batch_size:1 for text-gen-prod & rerank-prod
- set KV cache: disabled for those routes
- added routing policy: prefer-dedicated-pool if available, else cpu-fallback

ops-bot: Routing rule change applied (config id: rr-2026-042-1).

4m later — alex (oncall): errors down to 0.2% and latency normalized. no additional node restarts in last 12m. customer-impact: org-omega reported transient failures for ~8 minutes; alpha-saas had interrupted streams, support sent guidance for client-side retries.

katie (support): thanks — I'll update the status page and message the affected accounts with RCA in progress. ETA for full resolution?

maya (runtime): medium-term: we need to collect full kernel+driver traces and attempt to isolate if the race is triggered by specific sequence lengths or eviction patterns. propose a scheduled canary: deploy driver 535.24-hotfix to a small canary pool with heavy-eviction workload. if repro rate drops to zero, coordinate safe rollout.

jenna (product): agree. set communications cadence: customer update in 30m, follow-up with PS teams once we have driver traces.

diego (serving): open action items:
- ACTION-1: maya to lead kernel log collection + contact vendor (assigned)
- ACTION-2: alex to revert batch changes when safe and monitor (assigned)
- ACTION-3: ops to prepare cpu-fallback capacity and autoscale policy (ops-bot acknowledged)
- ACTION-4: support to send customer impact summary (katie assigned)

alex (oncall): creating postmortem stub INC-2026-042 in ops tracker and assigning owners. adding timeline and commands run.

incident-bot: INCIDENT INC-2026-042 status: mitigated -> partial. Next update by 2026-03-15T14:00Z.

jenna (product): thanks team. good job on quick mitigations. will track follow-ups in the postmortem. :thumbsup:

maya (runtime): one more note: if kernel team asks for reproducer, point them to repro-gpu-01 logs + ./scripts/stress_kv_cache.sh args + core dumps available at s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-042/cores/

alex (oncall): I'll attach artifacts. closing thread for now, will reopen if error rate increases. :white_check_mark:
